items.title: 53571_Mary Lou Williams oral history interview
items.q: Mr. Ripp was there, the manager of the Carnegie

ctx.x: a symphony. I don't know what I'm going to do. I need another tune." He said, "Oh, darling, you can do it. Go ahead, darling," and he kept saying that until I got on the floor and I started writing and I finished off "Scorpio". All of a sudden I decided I wanted them to play a blues. So I sat there and I made up a blues. I heard a record - I didn't copy all of Charlie Parker's solo but I said I better give them a bop thing because I'm going to give it to 36 violins. It was 100 pieces. So I wrote this blues and…
